commits.message:
Multi-line TextInput shows a zero-cell glyph as a one-cell stand-in, so every cursor stop draws a visible cell (rich-unfiled-791c.bynu) (#461)

* Multi-line TextInput shows a zero-cell glyph as a one-cell stand-in, so every cursor stop draws a visible cell (rich-unfiled-791c.bynu)

Rows stay slices of value; drawing, hit-testing and vertical motion measure
them through the same shown-as function single-line uses, and the wrap
strategy receives the line as shown so its budget counts the stand-ins. A
multi-line password field now masks its text as single-line does.

* A wrap row names the stretch of the line it draws, mapped back to the value in one pass, and TextInput measures the cells it draws (rich-unfiled-791c.bynu)

WrapRow is { start, end } in place of { content, start }. Since the
strategy started receiving the line as shown, the widget drew the matching
stretch of `value` and read only content's length, so a row whose content
was not a stretch of its line (a hyphen added at a break) drew repeated
glyphs. The type no longer admits such a row.

The shown-to-line offset table is built once per line, not walked from
the start for every row end: the guard read 16x for 4x input against the
walk. It also maps a stand-in of any length, not only one code unit.

measure() takes the widest shown line, so a zero-cell glyph counts its
one cell, a password counts a mask per glyph, and a multi-line value is
as wide as its widest line.
